name: ESTHER IDANG
feedback: D1 is a strong catalogue. You correctly classed nine of the ten planted findings with the right OWASP and CWE and a quoted evidence line for each, the SQL injection at login.php 64-67 reconciled to 02:15:31, the alg:none token at 48-49 tied to Token 2, the hardcoded secret at line 30, the missing exp, the stored XSS cookie beacon at 02:18:47, plus the full access-control set of path traversal at 02:24:02, open redirect at 02:21:13, and the Secure and SameSite cookie gap. Two things cost you here. You missed XXE as a standalone finding, and more importantly you named XXE as the decoy and disproved it, which is wrong. XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml with SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd is a genuine A05 CWE-611 finding, so you both lost that finding and lost the decoy row. The real decoy is the safe construct in the JWT helper, the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals, which is constant-time and sound, and the right move is to flag it tempting and prove it safe at the mechanism level while pointing at alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the actual bugs. D2 is excellent. The ten-hop chain is in order and every hop reconciles to a capture line or artefact, recon at 02:14:08, SQLi at 02:15:31, the 312-row pull at 02:16:04, XSS at 02:18:47, redirect at 02:21:13, the blocked XXE then path traversal at 02:24:02, ending on the CSV exfil. You gave verbatim PoCs per hop and complete CVSS vectors for all nine findings. The impact section is the standout, ₦59.9 million across 312 customers from a stated ₦192,011.59 average over 20 sample rows, flagged as a baseline pending the offline locker, and tied to the BoltCash launch in six weeks. To get the last marks, justify each CVSS vector with one sentence rather than only XSS and open redirect, and note your SQLi vector should be A:N not A:L since the auth bypass does not hit availability, which makes it about 9.1 rather than 9.4. D3 is clean and well structured, a jargon-free exec summary landing on customers and naira, a real threat model naming the Tor exit node and the shared internal auth, findings tied to evidence, a correct earliest-break fix at Hop 3, and remediation ordered by effort to risk rather than severity, which is exactly right, you ranked the 9.6 stored XSS at seven because it costs 6-12 hours while the cheap high-leverage SQLi fix leads. Your two stopgaps name the exact field, body.username and body.text, with concrete rules and a false-positive justification. The only deductions in D3 trace back to the same XXE gap and the wrong decoy verdict carried over from D1. D4 is full marks, all four prompts owned with a clear no-comment stance, ISC2 canons cited by number and load-bearing, the NDPA 2023 Part 6 section 40 breach duty tied to the 312 records, and a genuine personal anchor about confirming the forged super_admin Token 1 by re-running HS256 with openssl. The single most important fix is the decoy, learn to separate a safe mechanism like constant-time hash_equals from a real vulnerability like XXE, because mislabelling a live finding as the decoy is the one error that pulled this otherwise near-complete report down from the high 80s.
